title: Embeddings pricing heads-up and benchmark talking points (scratch)
content:
Purpose:
- Scratchpad for an internal heads-up note + quick all-hands talking points about an embeddings pricing adjustment and a set of benchmark highlights we want teams to know before external comms.
- Keep this informal: notes to self, Qs, suggested phrasing for comms, and who to ping.

Context (short):
- Optimize shipped the new batching + cache profile for popular embedding workloads (dense-sim use cases). Perf tests show ~35% lower avg cost per 1k vectors and 20% p50 latency improvement in our hosted cluster.
- Finance/product want to adjust list pricing tiers for embeddings (tier thresholds + unit price) to better reflect lower unit costs and capture value.
- We need an internal alignment note for GTM, Sales Ops, Solutions Eng, Support, and SRE before any external announcement.

Draft internal subject line (options):
- "Heads-up: Embeddings unit price & benchmark highlights (internal)"
- "Internal: Upcoming embeddings pricing & perf summary — FYI + Qs"

Draft short email (internal) — option A (concise):
Hi all,

Quick heads-up: we’re planning to adjust embeddings pricing and want you to have the benchmark highlights up front. Early summary: new Optimize profile reduces avg unit cost by ~35% on common workloads and improves p50 latency ~20%. We’re proposing modest list price changes to reflect lower costs while preserving gross margin.

Why you should care: Sales + SE should expect updated quoting guidance; Support should read the benchmark notes in case customers ask about perf differences; Infra/SRE should expect a small config rollout window next week.

See details below + linked artifacts. Please flag any immediate concerns by EOD Thu.

—Zoe

Longer draft email (for product + sales ops inbox):
Hi product/gtm/sales-ops,

Working draft: we recommend moving embeddings unit price from X -> Y for volumes > 100k vectors/month, and adjusting the mid tier thresholds. Rationale: Optimize cost improvements (benchmarks attached) allow us to reduce price slightly while keeping projected margin.

Attached: benchmark notes (short), cost model (CONF link), internal quote examples for top 10 customers.

Open Qs:
- Final margin target from Finance (asked @Priya, awaiting reply).
- Should we grandfather existing customers for n months or do immediate migration? (Sales ops preference?)
- External comms timeline — do we align with the Optimize minor release next week?

Action items:
- Marcus: finalize cost model and recommended price points (due Thu).
- Priya: confirm margin floor and approval process (due Fri).
- Omar: prepare SE FAQ with two example customer messages (due Fri).

All-hands / Leadership talking points (30–60s):
- Quick opener: "We’ve made targeted infrastructure and runtime improvements to our embeddings stack. Early results show material cost and latency improvements for common retrieval and similarity workloads."
- Why it matters: "Lower per-vector costs mean customers can embed more content for the same spend, and we can offer more competitive pricing while protecting margins."
- Reassurance: "No customer data changes, no model quality change — purely runtime and batching/cache improvements. We’ll provide guidance for any pricing transitions."
- Call to action: "If you work with customers on pricing / procurement, review the GTM note and flag anything we should raise in leadership syncs."

Anticipated internal Q&A (quick answers):
Q: Are we changing model or model quality?
A: No — model checkpoints and embedding vectors unchanged. This is serving/runtime acceleration and smarter batching + cache.

Q: Will customers see different vector outputs?
A: No. Outputs are identical. Only throughput/latency and cost per token/vector are improved.

Q: Will this break existing billings / accounting?
A: We’ll do price migration logic in billing platform (Sales ops leading). We expect a small number of edge cases — Finance will run retroactive checks.

Q: Who should Sales direct customers to?
A: SE + Solutions Eng first, then product if there are product-level questions. Pub contact: solutions-eng@redwood.ai (placeholder).

Notes to self / rough bench bullet points (for inclusion in a one-pager):
- Test harness: retrieval-sim synthetic + two real customer workloads (legal-search, support-search).
- Metrics: avg cost per 1k vectors: baseline $0.011 -> new $0.007 (approx -35%). p50 latency: baseline 42ms -> new 33ms. p95 roughly unchanged for long tails; we should call that out.
- Workload profile: benefits concentrated on small-to-medium vector sizes with steady request rates (bursty workloads see less improvement unless cached).
- Risk: caching introduces potential cold-start artifacts; SRE to monitor cache hit distributions and eviction patterns.

Unresolved / open questions (TO DECIDE):
- Grandfathering window length (0 / 30 / 90 days)? Pros/cons: immediate change = revenue quicker but more churn risk; 90d = easier for large customers.
- External messaging tone: "price reduction" vs "pricing realignment". Legal preference? (Ping legal).
- Internal rollout sequence: small cohort of customers + public announcement vs all-customer release.

Slack channels to ping once alignment done: #product-announce, #sales-ops, #solutions-eng, #sre-critical.

Draft SE FAQ (bullets):
- "What changed?" -> runtime improvements (batching/cache), same vectors.
- "How much cost savings?" -> up to ~35% on common workloads; depends on pattern.
- "Is this automatic?" -> Yes, customers on hosted API will benefit with no action. For Dedicated/Private: customers need to update their runtime config to get new profile (docs + upgrade notes forthcoming).
- "If a customer reports regressions?" -> Escalate to eng-applied-ml + bench team, open ticket JIRA-EMB-REGRESS. Capture prompt/ workload sample, timestamp, API version.

Communications timeline (proposal):
- Day 0 (internal): Send this heads-up to GTM + Support + SRE/infra.
- Day 3: Leadership finalizes price point + migration window.
- Day 5: Publish internal FAQ, prepare customer-facing KB + sales one-pager.
- Day 7: External announcement + blog post aligned with Optimize release notes.

Things to attach to the final internal note (links/placeholders):
- Short benchmark one-pager (CONF-OPTIMIZE-EMB-2026).
- Cost model calc (spreadsheet).
- Example customer migration plan (doc).
- Billing migration playbook (JIRA-PRICING-88).

Tone guidance (for comms):
- Keep it simple. Avoid technical overload in customer-facing materials. Internally, include perf numbers + variance and examples.
- Emphasize benefit to customers but be transparent about migration mechanics.

Reminders / TODOs (me):
- Pull 2 more real-customer workload runs for mid-tier customers (legal-search + marketplace).
- Schedule 20m sync with Marcus, Priya, Omar (calendar).
- Draft external blog outline after leadership sign-off.

Rough timeline notes (personal):
- If we want public sync with Optimize release (next Wed), need final pricing decisions by Fri (this week).
- If Finance pushes longer cycle, push public announcement 2 weeks later.

Random scratch/ideas to consider (brainstorm):
- Consider a temporary promo (first month free for extra embeddings) to drive adoption and avoid sticker shock. Pros: demonstrates value quickly. Cons: complicates billing/margin.
- Could show customers an "estimated savings" calculator in console (low dev effort if we reuse cost model).

Last line: save for internal review. This is a scratchpad — will convert to formal internal memo once Marcus+Priya confirm numbers.
